symptom: A $Type newer than the project was written with no version gate, and the project then did not load: exec reported success, then mx check 9.24.30 died with `TypeCacheUnknownTypeException: The type cache does not contain a type with qualified name Workflows$WaitForNotificationActivity` (a workflow with `wait for notification`) and `… Microflows$GetWorkflowsAction` (a microflow with `get workflows`). The fourth-plus recurrence of one class: #1754, #1209, #1163, #1771
cause: The generated version data (modelsdk/version, from modelsdk/gen/*/version.go) holds property versions only: version.TypeVersionInfo has no field for a type's own introduction, and the generated packages cannot be regenerated (hand fixes, #1163). So the write path compared every key with the project's version and never an element's $Type
file: `modelsdk/canon/typefloor.go` (UndeclaredTypeError, TypeIntroduced, TypeDeclared), `modelsdk/canon/mendixmodelsdk_type_versions.json` + `gen_type_versions.go` (extracted from mendixmodelsdk 4.117.0), `modelsdk/mpr/writer_property_sets.go` (normalizePropertySetsFor: after the lowering and the property floor, on the bytes that land), `mdl/executor/version_gates.go` (workflowTypeGates, workflowDefinitionSelectionGate)
insight: **Key the type floor by STORAGE name, and let an alias only loosen it.** The SDK names types by qualified name; the codec's storage aliases (modelsdk/gen/*/types.go SetTypeName) map them, but a storage name only an alias reaches can belong to an older type the SDK does not list: the first extraction floored Forms$FormCallArgument at 9.7 (alias of the SDK's PageParameterMapping) and refused 311 units Studio Pro 9.1.1 and 9.4.0 wrote. Each row is now the union of every SDK type stored under its name, and a name only an alias reaches gets no row. **The oracle for the data is Studio Pro-authored bytes across versions, and the Marketplace has a ladder of them**: Workflow Commons publishes a version per Mendix minor (9.24, 10.0, 10.3, 10.11, 10.12, 10.14, 10.17, 11.0, 11.2, 11.8, 11.9, 11.11, 11.13, 11.16), each .mpk holding a project.mpr; plus samples 117680 (9.4.0), 117785 (9.1.1), 221741 (9.24.3) and blank apps from the cached mxbuilds. `MXCLI_TYPEFLOOR_PROJECTS=<a.mpr>:<b.mpr> go test ./modelsdk/mpr -run TestTypeFloor_StoredProjectsHoldNoUndeclaredType` scans them: 23 projects, 0 refusals, after the alias fix. **A cached mxbuild is a second oracle, and needs no project**: `strings -a Mendix*.dll | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_\n' '\n' | sort -u` lists every class name a version has. WaitForNotificationActivity, WaitForTimerActivity, the three timer boundary events, both WorkflowDefinition*Selection types, GetWorkflowsAction and NotifyWorkflowAction are absent from 9.24.30's and present in 10.24.24's; of the 255 rows floored above 9.24, 224 short names are absent there. The 31 'present' are short-name collisions across a domain move (Rest$EntitySet is ODataPublish$EntitySet from 10.4, measured unloadable on 9.24 in #1163) or generic names (Line, Value, Source), so key on the domain before trusting a hit. **Do not enforce the SDK's deletion versions.** The same class-name list shows 56 SDK-deleted types still classes in 11.15.0's mxbuild, Workflows$UserTask, XPathBasedUserSource and TimerBoundaryEvent among them (kept to load and convert older models). A rename keeps the storage name (CallMicroflowTask 'deleted' 11.9 is still how every call microflow activity is stored), and mxbuild 11.x still loads Workflows$TimerBoundaryEvent, 'deleted' 10.20 (MDL-WF07 exists because only the RUNTIME lacks it). An introduction floor cannot misfire on a rename (the new name is never stored), a deletion floor can. **Order matters for the messages**: the type floor runs after the property floor, so a key a version lacks is still named as the key (CallMicroflowTask.BoundaryEvents on 10.13), and only a type with no older shape is refused as a type. Its first catch in the existing tests was a CONTROL that was wrong: a user task's InterruptingTimerBoundaryEvent was asserted writable on 10.14, but that is a 10.20 type (10.14–10.19 store TimerBoundaryEvent). The second: TestCreateWorkflow_AIAgentTaskRoundTrip wrote Workflows$AIAgentTaskActivity (11.9, absent from the 11.6 mxbuild) to the 11.6.6 fixture; it now sets the fixture to 11.14.0, and the 11.6.6 refusal is its own test. Measured: 9.24.30 fresh apps, before → TypeCacheUnknownTypeException for WaitForNotificationActivity and GetWorkflowsAction; after → check -p MDL-VERSION01 for the first, write refusal 'cannot store Microflows$GetWorkflowsAction (Mendix 10.4.0+)' for the second, App.mpr byte-identical, mx check 0 errors. Bug-test on 10.24.24 and 11.13.0: exec and mx check identical before/after, 0 errors. Doctype suite on 9.24.30 before and after: 61 pass, the same 17 fail at the same first failure (none of them a type), and no TypeCacheUnknownTypeException either way: every script that would write a newer type is @version-gated or fails earlier, which is how the class kept shipping. Run UNFILTERED instead (every doctype script into one fresh app, exec --continue-on-error --no-check, so gates still refuse what they cover): on 9.24.30 the floor refuses Rest$ODataEntityTypeSource (10.8, external entities from OData), Microflows$RestOperationCallAction (10.1), NotifyWorkflowAction (10.0), GetWorkflowsAction and GetWorkflowActivityRecordsAction (10.4), none of them gated; on 10.24.24 it refuses no type, and none of the new gates fires. **The SDK introduction can be later than the platform class**: 9.24.30 loads a RestOperationCallAction (mx check: CE7053 "No REST operation specified", no load failure) though the SDK says 10.1; its target (Rest$ConsumedRestService, 10.1) is absent from 9.24, so the activity cannot be configured there and refusing it costs nothing, but a floor is a claim about loading, so measure before lowering one. Control: replacing the UndeclaredTypeError call with nil fails the five new/changed tests with the write accepted. Tests: writer_type_floor_1774_test.go, type_floor_projects_test.go, canon/typefloor_test.go, version_gates_workflow_types_1774_test.go; mdl-examples/bug-tests/1774-workflow-types-below-their-version.mdl
